title: Turning Zeeman splitting into switchable charge polarization in a double quantum dot
abstract: A magnetic field that acts identically on two quantum dots is not expected to move charge between them. Nevertheless, we show that a uniform Zeeman field can strongly reconfigure and even reverse the single-electron charge polarization of an asymmetric open double quantum dot. Using a symmetry-preserving Green's-function equation-of-motion approach, we identify regimes where the preferred dot occupation reverses while the system remains in the single-electron charge sector. Two distinct mechanisms produce this behavior. Unequal gate levels produce different occupation responses because the Zeeman-shifted resonances lie at different positions relative to the reservoir chemical potential, whereas unequal onsite interactions distinguish the dots through their many-body addition spectra. Coulomb blockade stabilizes the single-electron sector, causing the reservoir-mediated response to appear as spatial charge redistribution rather than a change in total occupation. Our results establish a mechanism for magnetic control of charge polarization at fixed electrostatic detuning.
summary: This theoretical study demonstrates that a uniform magnetic field can be used to switch the charge polarization between two quantum dots, even if the dots are otherwise symmetric. This control arises because the coupling to external reservoirs and the presence of Coulomb interactions allow the uniform spin splitting to manifest as a directional charge bias. The findings establish a robust mechanism for magnetic control of charge qubits.
main_problem: To determine if a uniform Zeeman field can induce a controllable left-right charge polarization in an asymmetric double quantum dot (DQD), contrary to initial expectations.
main_result: The authors show that in an open, interacting DQD, the uniform Zeeman field can strongly reconfigure and even reverse the single-electron charge polarization through mechanisms involving unequal gate levels or unequal onsite interactions.
method: The study employs a symmetry-preserving Green's-function Equation-of-Motion (EOM) approach, solving for density correlators up to three-body terms to reconstruct the full probability distribution over the system's Fock states.
model_or_system: The system is an open, interacting double quantum dot (DQD) coupled to electronic reservoirs. The Hamiltonian includes intra-dot and inter-dot Coulomb repulsions, and the magnetic field enters via Zeeman splitting, $M_z$.
key_observables: Left-localized probability ($P_L$), right-localized probability ($P_R$), and the resulting charge polarization $D = P_L - P_R$.
important_parameters: Zeeman field strength ($M_z$), gate detuning ($v_1 - v_2$), and onsite interaction differences ($U_1 - U_2$).
main_assumptions: The EOM hierarchy is truncated, and the authors use a symmetry-preserving closure technique to ensure the calculated correlators are free from artificial route dependence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnetic field dependence of charge reconfiguration ($\Delta P_{	ext{max}}$) for both unequal gate levels and unequal onsite interactions, showing the switching behavior of $P_L$ and $P_R$ versus $M_z$.
paper_structure:
The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using the EOM approach, then analyzes the case of level asymmetry ($v_1 
eq v_2$), followed by the case of interaction asymmetry ($U_1 
eq U_2$), concluding with a discussion of the underlying physics of open-system conversion.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical mechanism for controlling charge polarization using magnetic fields in strongly correlated nanoscale systems, which is highly relevant for quantum computing architectures based on charge qubits.
